freeze_statement: This file is FROZEN on write. It is the pre-screen gate required by TASK-20260801-806's first constraint. No candidate verdict in this file was revised after any derivation was written or any code was executed. The derivation artifact (od4_branching_bound_report.md), the source artifact (od4_branching.py) and the results manifest (od4_results.json) were all created AFTER this file.
honesty_note_on_ordering: Stated precisely so an independent reviewer can check the claim rather than take it. (i) NOTHING was written to disk in this task's directory before this file, and NO code was written or executed before this file: the results manifest records the file creation order and the first command timestamp. (ii) Assigning an interface constant to a candidate necessarily requires reading the shape of the argument the candidate would run -- that reading is exactly what the screen asks for and it happened before this file, as it must. (iii) What did NOT happen before this file is any derivation, any lemma, any computation, or any artifact. (iv) The two candidates recorded IN_SCOPE_VACUOUS below were not developed further in any artifact of this task; the report states this per candidate.

screen_definition.question_b: Does the candidate's argument spread invariance -- or any other propagated property -- through the directed (lambda,k) graph on {(lambda,k) : lambda in GF(2^8)^*, k in {0,1,2,3}} or through its square G^2?
screen_definition.question_c: If yes: the INTERFACE CONSTANT n, being the number of consecutive super-box interfaces over which the tracked object must survive before the argument concludes anything.
screen_definition.threshold: PURSUE iff n <= about 7. IN_SCOPE_VACUOUS iff n > about 7, or if no upper bound on n can be exhibited.
screen_definition.threshold_basis: RQ-AES-001 scopes in-scope round counts to 3-7. Under PROP-701-I's own one-interface-per-round modelling convention an in-scope argument gets at most 7 interfaces. TASK-20260801-801 measured the (lambda,k) graph's geometry exactly (forward and reverse diameter 30, radius 30, eccentricity distribution {30: 1020}, G^2 diameter 16, covering number n* = 15, vertex-transitive), and Proposition 801-1's interface constant of 2 + 2n* = 32 is the cheapest constant that machine can produce. DEC-20260731-014 ruled Proposition 801-1 IN-SCOPE VACUOUS on exactly that margin, AFTER it was proved.
screen_definition.conversion_caveat: The one-interface-per-round identification is PROP-701-I's own modelling convention (residual R5) and is NOT established by anything in this campaign. This pre-screen therefore applies the threshold under BOTH conversions, recorded per candidate in `verdict_under_alternative_conversion`. The alternative conversion considered is ONE INTERFACE PER SUPER-BOX = TWO ROUNDS, under which an in-scope argument at 7 rounds gets at most 3 (floor(7/2) = 3) interfaces. That conversion is STRICTLY TIGHTER than PROP-701-I's, so no candidate can pass under it that fails under PROP-701-I's, and every PURSUE below is checked to survive n <= 3 as well. No conversion known to this task makes MORE than 7 interfaces available inside RQ-AES-001's round scope, so the about-7 threshold is used as the binding one.
screen_definition.anti_relabelling_clause: The screen is on the argument's ITERATION COUNT OVER INTERFACES however the iteration is packaged. Packaging n graph steps inside one lemma does not change n. Each candidate below states where its iteration count comes from, not merely its value.

candidates.statement: Re-run PROP-701-I's Steps 1-3 verbatim with the equality pi(u) = pi(u+v) replaced throughout by the weaker B-confinement 'pi(u) and pi(u+v) lie in a common set of size at most B', and close the resulting translation structure under the group it generates, as Step 3 does.
candidates.where_the_iteration_count_comes_from: Step 3 is precisely a traversal of the directed (lambda,k) graph: it must reach every (lambda,k) node from the starting node before it may conclude that the translation set spans F^4 and hence that pi is constant. Each application of Steps 1-2 that advances the traversal consumes one super-box interface, because Step 1's hypothesis is a statement about pi across ONE application of Phi. The count is therefore the traversal length, not a packaging choice.
candidates.interface_constant_basis: TASK-20260801-801's measured forward diameter of the directed (lambda,k) graph is 30 and its eccentricity distribution is {30: 1020}, so 30 is not merely an upper bound: EVERY node has a node at distance exactly 30 from it, and the graph is vertex-transitive, so no choice of starting node reduces it. Using G^2 as Proposition 801-1 does gives 2 + 2n* = 32, which is worse, not better. 30 is therefore the cheapest constant available to this candidate and it is exhibited, not estimated.
candidates.verdict_margin: 30 interfaces required against at most 7 available: a margin of 23 interfaces, of the same order as the 24-interface margin on which DEC-20260731-014 ruled Proposition 801-1 in-scope vacuous.
candidates.verdict_under_alternative_conversion: IN_SCOPE_VACUOUS (30 against at most 3 available; the alternative conversion is strictly worse for this candidate).
candidates.pursuit_statement: NOT PURSUED. No lemma, derivation or computation for this candidate appears in any artifact of this task. Recorded and stopped.

candidates.statement: Type-level analysis of PROP-701-I's Step-1-to-Step-2 bootstrap under bounded branching: determine whether the conclusion Step 1 produces under B > 1 is of the same logical type as the hypothesis Step 1 consumes, which is what licenses Step 2 to re-apply Step 1 to the derived pair and what makes the whole argument an induction.
candidates.what_machine_it_routes_through_instead: It routes through NO propagation machine at all. It is a statement about ONE application of Step 1 and the single re-application attempted at the start of Step 2, both inside a SINGLE super-box interface: Step 1 consumes a hypothesis of the form 'pi(a) = pi(b)' and, under B > 1, emits a conclusion of the form 'pi(u) and pi(u+v) lie in a common set of size at most B'. Whether those two types match is decided by inspecting the two statements against each other; no traversal, no closure, no iteration and no second interface is involved, and the (lambda,k) graph is never entered because the graph is only reached in Step 3, which this candidate never gets to. The interface screen does not apply because the argument's iteration count over interfaces is 1 by construction: it examines the FIRST step of the induction and asks whether that step closes. If it does not close, the argument terminates at interface 1 and every downstream count is moot. This is substantive rather than a label: it names the exact two statements compared (Step 1's hypothesis and Step 1's conclusion under B > 1), names the property being tested between them (type identity, i.e. whether the conclusion can serve as the hypothesis of the next application), and names why no further interface can be consumed (the induction is refuted or confirmed at its first step).

candidates.statement: Compute exactly, at ONE interface, the minimal branching factor B forced on an F-linear per-word projection pi : F^4 -> F^4/K by the algebra of Phi = ARK . MC . SR, as a function of the kernel K, and minimise it over all K to obtain an unconditional lower bound on B for the F-linear subclass.
candidates.what_machine_it_routes_through_instead: It routes through the COORDINATE-SUPPORT AND MINOR STRUCTURE OF THE MIXCOLUMNS MATRIX M inside a single interface, not through any propagation. Concretely: ShiftRows makes output word j collect its row-i pre-MixColumns coordinate from input word (j+i) mod 4, so the four coordinates of the unknown pre-MixColumns perturbation of a single output word are drawn from FOUR DIFFERENT input words and are therefore free of one another. The perturbation set is consequently the product of the coordinate projections of K, MixColumns carries that product to the F-span of the corresponding columns of M, and the branching is the cardinality of the image of that span under pi. Every quantity in that chain is a finite linear-algebra invariant of M and K -- which coordinates of K are nonzero, and what dimension the corresponding column span meets K in -- and each is settled by a finite exhaustive check on M (all entries nonzero; all minors nonzero, i.e. the MDS property; the intersection dimensions of column spans with coordinate subspaces). No property is propagated from one interface to the next, so no traversal length exists and the interface screen has nothing to count: the argument concludes from ONE interface. The (lambda,k) graph is not entered, and is not needed, because the argument never asks what translations leave pi invariant -- it asks how large the image of a known subspace is, which is a dimension computation.

candidates.statement: Compose the one-interface bound of CAND-806-C over n consecutive interfaces and over the four super-box words of the state, and set the resulting per-attempt tracking cost against the trivial state-enumeration baseline to obtain a cost inequality in n.
candidates.what_machine_it_routes_through_instead: It routes through ARITHMETIC ON A COST MODEL, with n a FREE PARAMETER OF THE TABLE rather than a constant the argument must reach before it says anything. The distinction is the whole point of the screen and is stated substantively: CAND-806-A must traverse 30 interfaces before its conclusion exists at all, so at n = 7 it says nothing; CAND-806-D has a complete statement at EVERY n >= 1 -- at n = 1 it says the per-interface tracking cost is at least B^4, at n = 3 it says B^{12}, and so on -- and the only thing that changes with n is which side of the baseline the number lands on. No property is propagated and no closure is taken; the same one-interface inequality is multiplied, and the multiplication is an assumption about the cost model that is recorded as a NUMBERED HEURISTIC rather than as a derivation. Its required interface count is therefore 1, being the count at which its underlying inequality is already true and reportable. This candidate is admitted only because CAND-806-C is admitted; if CAND-806-C returned nothing, this would have nothing to compose.
candidates.verdict_under_alternative_conversion: PURSUE (n = 1 <= 3). Note the cost table is reported at every n in 1..7 under both conversions so the reader can read off either.

candidates.statement: Treat the B-confinement relation produced by Step 1 under B > 1 as an approximate-symmetry structure and grow it by an approximate-group / Freiman-type closure argument, recovering an approximate version of Step 3's group closure and hence a lower bound on B from the growth rate required to fill F^4.
candidates.where_the_iteration_count_comes_from: This candidate does not avoid Step 3's traversal; it replaces exact closure with approximate closure and must still fill the SAME (lambda,k) graph, because the translations it is growing are exactly the lambda m_k of Step 3. Its iteration count is therefore AT LEAST the traversal length of the exact argument, and strictly greater in general: an approximate-closure step advances the reachable set less than an exact one does, so the number of interfaces consumed to reach a given node is bounded below by the exact distance and is not bounded above by anything this task can exhibit, since the loss per step depends on B and on the (unknown) overlap structure of the confining sets.
candidates.interface_constant_statement: NO UPPER BOUND ON n COULD BE EXHIBITED. A lower bound of 30 is available (the measured forward diameter, which the approximate argument cannot beat, since approximate closure advances no faster than exact closure through the same edge set). An upper bound would require quantifying the per-step loss of the approximate closure, which this task did not do and which is not obviously finite.
candidates.verdict_margin: Killed on TWO independent grounds, either sufficient: (i) no upper bound on n exhibited, which the screen's rule (d) makes an automatic IN_SCOPE_VACUOUS; (ii) the exhibited LOWER bound of 30 already exceeds the 7 available.
candidates.pursuit_statement: NOT PURSUED. No lemma, derivation or computation for this candidate appears in any artifact of this task. Recorded and stopped.

candidates.statement: Ask whether a counting or entropy argument over the fibres of an ARBITRARY (not necessarily linear) per-word projection pi forces a lower bound on B at one interface, in terms of the entropy loss L alone.
candidates.what_machine_it_routes_through_instead: It routes through FIBRE COUNTING inside a single interface. The object examined is the set of output words reachable from a fixed input pi-profile: that set is determined by the byte-i coordinate projections of the four relevant fibres of pi, carried through M, and the branching is the size of its pi-image. The argument is a cardinality comparison between that image and the fibre size 2^L; it propagates nothing, iterates nothing, and concludes -- affirmatively or negatively -- from one interface. The interface screen does not apply because there is no traversal to count; the count is 1. This is substantive rather than a label: it names the object counted (byte-coordinate projections of pi-fibres), the inequality attempted (image size at least set size divided by maximal fibre size), and the exact place the counting can fail (a fibre of size 2^L can lie inside a single fixed-byte coset, driving a coordinate projection to size 1), which is a one-interface fact about pi and not a propagation fact.
candidates.expected_outcome_preregistered: This candidate is admitted with the explicit expectation, recorded BEFORE it is worked, that it may return NO BOUND. That outcome is reported as the result and is not treated as a failure.
